query: Can private defence be used against a public servant?

gold_references.label: Section 37
gold_references.role: no right of private defence against public servant acting in good faith under colour of office

acceptable_references.label: Section 35
acceptable_references.reason: general scope of right of private defence

required_points: Section 37 provides that there is no right of private defence against an act which does not reasonably cause the apprehension of death or grievous hurt, if done or attempted to be done by a public servant acting in good faith under colour of his office, even if that act may not be strictly justifiable by law.
However, if the act by a public servant does reasonably cause apprehension of death or grievous hurt, the right of private defence may still be exercised.
forbidden_points: Private defence can always be used against a public servant.
There is never any right of private defence against a public servant.

notes: Multi-hop. Section 37 limits private defence against public servants acting in good faith.
